newsitem.title: ITALY: Outrage after bathers damage famous Rome fountain.
newsitem.headline: Outrage after bathers damage famous Rome fountain.

text.p: Damage caused to a famous Rome fountain by three men who dived off part of its 17th-century Bernini sculpture on Tuesday outraged Italians and authorities promised tougher measures against vandalism.

The three were arrested after they took a dip in the fountain in the elegant Piazza Navona, snapping off a one-metre (three-foot) long piece from the tail of a dragon of the Four Rivers sculture by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, witnesses said.
Some 250 Italian and foreign tourists had been caught bathing in Rome's plethora of fountains in recent months.
Italian authorities, already smarting over a long line of damage to art treasures across the country, said on Tuesday laws would be tightened to deter further vandalism.
Culture Minister Walter Veltroni said a bill was already before parliament which would increase the maximum jail sentence for damaging public monuments from one to three years.
"I hope that, in the light of this latest episode, the law, presented in October 1996, can be approved quickly," Veltroni said in a statement.
In a move to deter other people from cooling off in public fountains, Rome's city council said anyone taking a dip from Wednesday would face an increased fine of one million lire ($560).

"After this latest, unforgiveable damage on the fountain of the Four Rivers, the moment has come to say 'enough' and punish those who show disregard for a cultural heritage unique in the world like that of Rome," the council said in a statement.
The three men, all from Rome, could face up to a year in jail for damaging the work of art on top of an automatic fine of 150,000 lire ($83) for swimming in a fountain, a police spokesman said.
One told police he had jumped into the water as temperatures in the Italian capital soared over 30 degrees Celsius (86 Fahrenheit). The men were aged between 33 and 43, police said.
The Rome council said the Four Rivers fountain, one of Bernini's most celebrated works, could be repaired after an Irish tourist retrieved the three pieces of the broken tail from the water.
The fountain, which towers above the square's chic cafes and is topped by an Egyptian obelisk, includes allegorical figures of the Nile, Danube, Ganges and Rio Plate rivers.
Earlier this month, a Danish tourist caused a scandal after wading topless through the baroque Trevi Fountain and a French student was arrested for bathing in the central Piazza Venezia.
In June, vandals attacked Florence's marble Fountain of Neptune for the second time this year, snapping a hoof off one of the horses which guard the basin.
